sources.population: 67 untrained college students (40 men, 27 women).
sources.protocol: Four technique practice sessions, tested 1RM and repetitions to fatigue for bench press, squat and deadlift; seven equations compared.
sources.supports: Studying repetition-based estimated 1RM under a specified protocol, not universal accuracy.
sources.limitations: High correlations coexisted with biased estimates; all equations underestimated deadlift. Sets with RIR >0, arbitrary exercises and trained populations are not established by this study.
sources.verification: Publisher abstract read; equation identity/context cross-checked in indexed paper text. No claim that every Epley output here was validated.

sources.supports: Separating a training stimulus/log from actual longitudinal muscle-size change.
sources.limitations: Recorded kg-repetitions and direct sets do not measure muscle cross-sectional area. No support here for the demo's 3/12-set reward cuts.
sources.verification: Publisher abstract and publication metadata read; no claim of full-text dose review.

rules.limitations: The exact 7/10 cut is provisional; soreness is not an injury diagnosis.

rules.title: HRV percentage-change flag
rules.population: No calibrated AthleteOS population. Source-specific populations must not be generalized automatically.
rules.protocol: Raw HRV ms with declared index/device/recording protocol when available; never relabel as lnRMSSD.
rules.limitations: Unknown comparability stays unknown. A <-20% change is not a universal meaningful or adverse HRV change.

rules.title: Resting-HR change flag
rules.population: No calibrated AthleteOS population. Source-specific populations must not be generalized automatically.
rules.protocol: Recorded resting HR; compare declared matching device/protocol where available.
rules.limitations: The +7 bpm cut is provisional. Hydration, environment, position and training context may confound interpretation.

rules.title: Weekly-load change flag
rules.population: No calibrated AthleteOS population. Source-specific populations must not be generalized automatically.
rules.protocol: Seven complete daily loads versus the preceding 28-day weekly average; zero/missing baseline gives no change.
rules.limitations: The +30% flag is uncalibrated and not a causal injury predictor. This is not ACWR.

rules.title: Composite demo readiness and modes
rules.population: No calibrated AthleteOS population. Source-specific populations must not be generalized automatically.
rules.protocol: Unweighted average of available component scores, without fitted outcome labels or calibrated weights.
rules.limitations: Every score transform and mode cut is a product heuristic. Readiness is not a probability or a performance forecast.

rules.title: Product dose recommendation
rules.population: No calibrated AthleteOS population. Source-specific populations must not be generalized automatically.
rules.protocol: Preserve original plan; use a gentle walk on a demo reduction; planned rest stays rest.
rules.limitations: No reviewed source establishes these exact 40%/60% reductions or guarantees injury prevention.

rules.title: Recorded strength stimulus

parameters.formula: sum(sets * reps * kg); sum direct sets by declared muscle

rules.population: No calibrated AthleteOS population. Source-specific populations must not be generalized automatically.
rules.protocol: One recorded exercise per daily workout; only direct sets, no inferred indirect stimulus.
rules.limitations: Volume and sets do not measure hypertrophy or equal optimal individual training dose.

rules.title: Epley formula estimate
rules.population: No calibrated AthleteOS population. Source-specific populations must not be generalized automatically.

rules.limitations: A formula output for RIR >0 or an arbitrary exercise is not a validated tested max. High correlation does not eliminate bias.

rules.title: Observed pace comparison
rules.population: No calibrated AthleteOS population. Source-specific populations must not be generalized automatically.
rules.protocol: Minutes/km; group by demo RPE 3-5; terrain/weather and measurement devices unknown.
rules.limitations: The comparability filters are product choices. No performance forecast or physiological adaptation follows from this trend.

rules.title: Micro Win product rules
rules.population: No calibrated AthleteOS population. Source-specific populations must not be generalized automatically.

sources.title: A New Approach to Monitoring Exercise Training
sources.population: Cycle exercise participants and basketball players; Haddad's review reports 12 cycle participants and 14 male basketball players.
sources.protocol: Steady-state/interval cycling and basketball; whole-session RPE compared with an HR-derived load method.
sources.supports: Quantifying internal session load, not an individual injury-risk threshold.
sources.limitations: Absolute RPE-derived and HR-derived scores differed despite consistent relationships. No validation of this app's readiness or dose reductions.
sources.verification: Publisher abstract read; sample details cross-checked in Haddad review table 2.

sources.title: Session-RPE Method for Training Load Monitoring: Validity, Ecological Usefulness, and Influencing Factors
sources.population: 36 validity/reliability studies across sports, ages, genders and training levels.
sources.protocol: Familiarized whole-session modified CR-10 ratings multiplied by minutes; review also describes monotony and strain.
sources.supports: sRPE calculation and descriptive derived load methods.
sources.limitations: RPE depends on collection protocol and other influences. Correlation/reliability do not establish causal injury prevention or universal load-change cuts.
sources.verification: Full-text rationale, derived calculations, validation discussion and table 2 read.

sources.title: Sleep and the athlete: narrative review and 2021 expert consensus recommendations
sources.population: Athlete literature, especially elite athletes; underrepresentation of females noted.
sources.protocol: Narrative synthesis and expert sleep toolbox; emphasizes individual perceived sleep needs and assessment validity.
sources.supports: Considering sleep in athlete monitoring and individualizing interpretation.
sources.limitations: Effects of partial restriction over 1-3 nights remain unclear; experimental control and measurement limitations. Does not validate <6 h, an 8 h score denominator or an automatic dose reduction.
sources.verification: Institutional repository abstract read; publisher page returned 403. No claim of full-text review.

sources.title: Monitoring training status with HR measures: do all roads lead to Rome?
sources.population: Aerobic-oriented athlete examples across recreational and elite settings; not a universal population calibration.
sources.protocol: Repeated standardized resting HR/HRV recordings; considers position, timing, HRV index, measurement error and training context.
sources.supports: Within-athlete monitoring with measurement comparability, variability and contextual interpretation.
sources.limitations: HRV can increase with worse wellness or decrease while performance improves. Raw unspecified HRV ms is not interchangeable with lnRMSSD. Descriptive SD is not measurement error or a clinically meaningful change.
sources.verification: Full-text abstract, recording conditions, table 1 and contradictory acute/chronic response sections read.

sources.title: Monitoring the athlete training response: subjective self-reported measures trump commonly used objective measures: a systematic review
sources.population: 56 original studies of athletes in training.
sources.protocol: Concurrent repeated subjective and objective well-being measures; established questionnaires with published validity/reliability, not arbitrary new scales.
sources.supports: Including repeated subjective well-being observations in monitoring.
sources.limitations: Subjective and objective measures generally did not correlate; heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Does not validate this app's custom 0-10 cuts or composite score.
sources.verification: Full-text abstract, selection criteria, synthesis and results read.

sources.title: Acute:Chronic Workload Ratio: Conceptual Issues and Fundamental Pitfalls
sources.population: Critique of ACWR literature, not a trial of this app or its uncoupled weekly comparison.
sources.protocol: Examines ratio construction, statistical artifacts and the causal inference needed to prescribe load for injury reduction.
sources.supports: Caution against converting load associations into causal injury-prevention claims.
sources.limitations: No established causal injury-reduction effect of manipulating ACWR. This app's weekly-change formula is not the same metric; the critique does not itself validate or directly test its +30% cut.
sources.verification: Indexed abstract verified through Europe PMC API, PMID 32502973; publisher access returned 403.

sources.title: Training Load and Its Role in Injury Prevention, Part 2: Conceptual and Methodologic Pitfalls
sources.population: Critical discussion of heterogeneous training-load/injury studies; not a validation cohort or an intervention trial.
sources.protocol: Examines exposure measures, ratios, time windows, categorization, injury definitions, analyses, generalizability and missing data.
sources.supports: Contextual review of load together with athlete responses; avoid treating associations, load changes or thresholds as causal injury evidence.
sources.limitations: Does not validate this app's weekly comparison, coincident-signal criterion, readiness, or 40%/60% dose factors. No injury probability or prevention benefit follows.
sources.verification: Full-text abstract, introductory practical scope, reference conceptual framework, and methodological sections on exposures, ratios, load measures, time windows, discretization, injury definitions, analyses, sample size, missing data and reporting read on 2026-11-15. Corrigendum (2021-05-17) read: acknowledges complementary overlapping commentary and omitted citation, not new threshold validation.

sources.title: The Accuracy of Prediction Equations for Estimating 1-RM Performance in the Bench Press, Squat, and Deadlift
sources.population: 67 untrained college students (40 men, 27 women).
sources.protocol: Four technique practice sessions, tested 1RM and repetitions to fatigue for bench press, squat and deadlift; seven equations compared.
sources.supports: Studying repetition-based estimated 1RM under a specified protocol, not universal accuracy.
sources.limitations: High correlations coexisted with biased estimates; all equations underestimated deadlift. Sets with RIR >0, arbitrary exercises and trained populations are not established by this study.
sources.verification: Publisher abstract read; equation identity/context cross-checked in indexed paper text. No claim that every Epley output here was validated.

sources.title: Resistance Training Recommendations to Maximize Muscle Hypertrophy in an Athletic Population: Position Stand of the IUSCA
sources.population: Athletic resistance-training context, synthesized by an expert consortium.
sources.protocol: Distinguishes constructs of hypertrophy, acute versus longitudinal evidence and strength versus hypertrophy.
sources.supports: Separating a training stimulus/log from actual longitudinal muscle-size change.
sources.limitations: Recorded kg-repetitions and direct sets do not measure muscle cross-sectional area. No support here for the demo's 3/12-set reward cuts.
sources.verification: Publisher abstract and publication metadata read; no claim of full-text dose review.
